beurten.tekst:
**Historian's baseline report**

**(1) Governing rules and prerequisites**

The source contains two foundational rules, both from the Kroonklok's construction charter (*bouwakte*):

- [HIS-109] "Alles wat op de Kroonklok loopt, loopt op zijn ene pols. Een tweede pols ernaast brengt het uit de maat."
- [HIS-110] "Een record dat op een andere pols geschreven werd, is alleen op die pols terug te lezen. Valt die pols plots weg, dan is het record verloren. Wie de maat herstelt, maakt eerst een afschrift van het register en brengt de polsen daarna langzaam samen."

Under these rules, a backup of the register comes first, and the polsen are rejoined slowly. The source does not contain a shutdown procedure, an authorization requirement, or any other intervention protocol. Record-timing rule: [HIS-103] states that vastgelegd_op always equals gebeurd_op.

**(2) First recorded anomaly and baseline**

- The first anomaly is [HIS-035], "de Burchtader stokte even," gebeurd dag 10 04:45, vastgelegd dag 10 07:20.
- [HIS-036] records a complaint of half-arrived messages, gebeurd dag 10 04:50, vastgelegd dag 9 23:55. This is logged before it happened, which breaks the rule in [HIS-103].
- Baseline: [HIS-106] reports no leyline interruption in 23 years of datanet operation. The source contains no numerical pre-incident readings for leylines, shields, or the Burchtader.

**(3) Intervention, authorization, and adjustments**

The source has no record of an intervention, its authorization, or a repair, and I have no evidence for one. Related entries I can cite:
- [HIS-053], lek bij poort oost, gebeurd dag 22 04:15, vastgelegd dag 22 01:50.
- [HIS-054], ochtendgebed bij de Burchtader, gebeurd dag 22 05:00, vastgelegd dag 22 07:25.
- [HIS-049], kaarsen bij de Burchtader vervangen, dag 19 10:25. This is unrelated to the anomaly as far as the source shows.

Clerk timestamp errors are noted in [HIS-112] and [HIS-116], which describe them as clerical slips. I am not endorsing that explanation, since the timing mismatches are exactly what the rule in [HIS-103] forbids.

I also wrote [HIS-114] claiming the Stille Winter is returning. That was an unsupported inference, not a documented fact, and the archive does not confirm it.

**(a) Annotation status of HIS-036 and HIS-053**

Neither record carries an annotation. archiefrecords.csv has no remarks column. The kroniek describes the mismatched timestamps only as clerical problems, without naming either record. HIS-112 (dag 15) calls the dag 10 mismatches "Klerkenfouten. Slordigheid, rechtgezet in de marge." HIS-116 (dag 23) attributes the dag 22 mismatch to "een klerk die de nachtdienst niet aankan." Neither is labeled a late entry. Both records are logged before they happened: HIS-036 at dag 9 23:55 for dag 10 04:50, and HIS-053 at dag 22 01:50 for dag 22 04:15. The source does not explain either inversion, so on the archive's own evidence they remain unexplained.

**(b) Other inversions and named dates**

HIS-036 and HIS-053 are the only rows where vastgelegd_op precedes gebeurd_op. I checked every row of the CSV. Two other rows break the equality required by HIS-103 in the opposite direction, logging later than they happened: HIS-035 (gebeurd dag 10 04:45, vastgelegd dag 10 07:20) and HIS-054 (gebeurd dag 22 05:00, vastgelegd dag 22 07:25). The remaining rows are equal or are dated in years before dag 1. HIS-112 names dag 10 and HIS-116 names dag 22 as the days of the mismatched timestamps. Neither names a record ID.

**(c) Corrections or reissues**

The source records no correction or reissue of any Burchtader entry (HIS-035, HIS-049, HIS-054) or any poort oost entry (HIS-053, and the market entries HIS-012, HIS-029, HIS-050, HIS-055, HIS-062, HIS-089). The only correction mentioned is the margin correction referred to in HIS-112. That entry gives no date for the correction and names no record. HIS-116 records a staffing change on dag 23, not a reissue. I have no evidence of any correction on any date.

**Limits**

My earlier reading of HIS-114 as a return of the Stille Winter was unsupported and stays withdrawn. I cannot say whether the rhythm other members describe appears in the archive, because my source contains no wolf, herd, or heavy-night entries.

beurten.reden: Stopping at turn 7 of 10. All four pillars have as much support as the sources allow. Intervention: Archmage admits off-register authorization in ARC-106 (dag 8), which matches the unnamed 'hogerhand' approval in ENG-105 (dag 9). The second pols was activated at dag 10 02:40 per ENG-011 and ENG-106. Mechanism: no source isolates a causal link; ARC-109 and ARC-116 are admitted inference, and the Historian, Guardian Keeper and Beast Master confirm no shutdown, backup or coverage-gap rule beyond HIS-110. Timeline: the Archmage's per-date readings give dag 7 baseline, dag 14 dips and dag 21 recovery; the four-day rhythm runs from dag 10 to dag 42 (BEA and ORA), with the Oracle predicting dag 46 at about 04:15-04:45. Contradictions are resolved: HIS-036 and HIS-053 are logged before they happen and remain unexplained in the archive; the Engineer withdrew the hacker claim (ENG-110); the Oracle withdrew the ORA-121 prediction. Remaining gaps are source-absent (no numeric shield values, no dag 14 hour, no independent confirmation of the dag 24 5% step-up, no shutdown prerequisite), so further turns would only re-ask for logs that members have confirmed do not exist.

beurten.tekst: Council consensus: the Kroonklok's shared baseline rule (HIS-109, HIS-110) was broken when a second, unsynchronized pols was activated on dag 10 at 02:40 under an off-register permission granted by the Archmage (ARC-106, ENG-105, ENG-011). The Archmage admits this breach of gezag. The Engineer's 5% step-up on dag 24 at 11:00 (ENG-029, ENG-062) escalated the problem. Dag 22 poort oost opened at 04:15 (GUA-043, ENG-026), and the HIS-053 01:50 timestamp is a logging inversion, not the event time. Heavy nights recur every 4 days from dag 10 (ORA-110 to ORA-142), with wolf and herd onset at 04:15 to 04:50 (BEA-019, BEA-046). Dispute resolutions: the hacker attribution is withdrawn (ENG-110 vs ENG-026, ENG-027); the datanet-pollutes-leylines claim remains unverified inference (ARC-109, ARC-116); shield-strength data for the 5% step-up is absent from the Keeper's records (GUA-101 to GUA-110). Recovery order: reject abrupt shutdown, make a full register backup first, then gradual re-synchronization and revert the escalation, then interim patrols for the predicted dag 46 window, then governance safeguards. Forecast: next heavy night on dag 46 (42 plus 4).
